title: Finite free domination of a standard etale algebra with prescribed prime lifts
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $f,g\in R[t]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], with $f$ monic (leading coefficient $1$), and put $B=(R[t]/(f))_{\bar g}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], where $\bar g$ is the class of $g$. Assume the class of the formal derivative $f'=\sum_{i\ge1}i a_i t^{i-1}$, for $f=\sum_i a_i t^i$, is a unit in $B$. Then there are a commutative $R$-algebra $C$ and an integer $r\ge0$ such that $C$ has an $R$-module basis indexed by $\{1,\ldots,r\}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is surjective [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Moreover, for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ and every prime ideal $\mathfrak q'\subset C$ with the same contraction to $R$, there exist $c\in C\setminus\mathfrak q'$ and an $R$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:B\to C_c$ such that $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q'C_c)=\mathfrak q$. If $R$ is nonzero, one can take $r\ge1$. Zero rings and constant monic $f$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 00UF, label lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, clauses (1)-(3); the proof constructs a finite free faithfully flat algebra by adjoining all roots, giving the stated finite free strengthening of clause (1).

proof.text: If $R=0$, take $C=0$ and $r=0$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\operatorname{Spec}C$ are empty, the structural map is surjective, and there are no primes $\mathfrak q$ or $\mathfrak q'$ to check. Assume henceforth that $R\ne0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-monic-finite-free-splitting-extension] to the monic polynomial $f$. We obtain a nonzero commutative $R$-algebra $C$, finite and free as an $R$-module, and elements $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n\in C$ such that the image of $f$ in $C[t]$ is $\prod_i(t-\alpha_i)$. The basis can be chosen finite: for finitely many module generators take the union of their finite coordinate supports in any free basis; if a basis vector were outside that union, it could not be in their span, by uniqueness of coordinates over the nonzero ring $R$. Reindex this finite basis by $\{1,\ldots,r\}$; since $C\ne0$, this basis is nonempty, so $r\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 00UF proof, first paragraph, using Tag 03HS (lemma-adjoin-roots)

proof.text: The structure map $R\to C$ is injective: if $a\mapsto0$, then multiplication by $a$ is zero on the free $R$-module $C$; evaluating it on any basis vector and using uniqueness of coordinates gives $a=0$. Because $C$ is finite as an $R$-module, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes $C$ integral over $R$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] gives surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. The chosen finite basis is exactly the asserted $R$-module basis indexed by $\{1,\ldots,r\}$.

source.place: Tag 00UF proof, clause (2), with integrality and lying-over written out

proof.text: Fix primes $\mathfrak q\subset B$ and $\mathfrak q'\subset C$ with common contraction $\mathfrak p\subset R$, and put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $L=\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Write $\lambda:C\to L$ for the residue map. Its kernel is $\mathfrak q'$: membership $d/1\in\mathfrak q'C_{\mathfrak q'}$ is equivalent, after clearing the finitely many denominators in a sum of ideal generators, to $sd\in\mathfrak q'$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak q'$; primality gives $d\in\mathfrak q'$. Conversely $d\in\mathfrak q'$ plainly has zero residue. Thus $R\to L$ has kernel $\mathfrak p$, and the formula $r/s\mapsto\lambda(r)/\lambda(s)$, $s\notin\mathfrak p$, descends to a unital map $k\to L$. Fractions with equal representatives have equal images by cross multiplication; elements of $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ map to zero. This makes $L/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Tag 00UF, label lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof; elementary details omitted in its final sentence supplied explicitly.

proof.text: Let $\rho:R[t]\to k[t]$ denote coefficient reduction and set $f_k=\rho(f)$, $g_k=\rho(g)$. Apply [lem-trf-localized-fibre-prime-factor] to $\mathfrak q$. It gives a monic irreducible $h\in k[t]$ with $h\mid f_k$, $h\nmid g_k$ and the explicit test $[P]/\bar g^{\,m}\in\mathfrak q\Longleftrightarrow h\mid\rho(P)$ for all $P\in R[t]$ and $m\ge0$. This supplies the localized-fibre prime/factor correspondence, including its contraction to the original ring, rather than treating it as part of the root-map universal property.

source.place: Tag 00UF, label lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof; elementary details omitted in its final sentence supplied explicitly.

proof.text: Put $a_i=\lambda(\alpha_i)\in L$. Coefficient reduction of the factorization of Step 1 yields $(f_k)_L=\prod_i(t-a_i)$: the map on coefficients preserves each finite sum and product in the convolution formula for polynomial multiplication [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and sends $t-\alpha_i$ to $t-a_i$. In particular it preserves the empty product. For any $P=\sum_j b_jt^j\in R[t]$, evaluation is compatible with the two coefficient maps by the explicit identity $\lambda(P(\alpha_i))=\sum_j\lambda(b_j)a_i^j=\rho(P)(a_i)$, where the last evaluation uses $k\to L$ from Step 3. Thus both the reduced splitting and the value of every polynomial use that same field embedding.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-residue-factor-root-selection] to $k\subset L$, $f_k,g_k,h$ and the factor list $a_i$ of Step 5. It supplies an index $i$ with $h(a_i)=0$ and $g_k(a_i)
e0$. Set $\alpha=\alpha_i$, $a=a_i$ and $c=g(\alpha)\in C$. Step 5 gives $\lambda(c)=g_k(a)
e0$, hence $c
otin\mathfrak q'$ by Step 3. Also $f(\alpha)=0$ by evaluating the factorization in $C$ at its $i$th root. In $C_c$, the image of $g(\alpha)=c$ is a unit. The hypothesis that $f'$ is invertible in $B$ is precisely the standard-etale pair condition stated in [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-pair-maps]. Its root-map universal property, applied to the image of $\alpha$ in $C_c$, gives the $R$-algebra map $\varphi:B	o C_c$. Explicitly it sends $[P]/ ar g^{\,m}$ to $P(\alpha)/c^m$.

proof.text: For every $H\in k[t]$, we claim $H(a)=0$ if and only if $h\mid H$. The forward implication has the following complete Bezout argument. If $h\nmid H$, every common divisor of $h,H$ is a unit: a nonunit divisor of the irreducible $h$ has a unit complementary factor, so is associated to $h$ and would force $h\mid H$. By the equivalence stated in [def-weil-coprime-polynomials], there are $U,V\in k[t]$ with $Uh+VH=1$. If $H(a)=0$, evaluation in $L$ gives $1=U(a)h(a)+V(a)H(a)=0$, a contradiction. Conversely $H=hJ$ immediately gives $H(a)=h(a)J(a)=0$. Thus the evaluation kernel over the residue field is exactly $(h)$, including for $H=0$.

source.place: Tag 00UF, label lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof; elementary details omitted in its final sentence supplied explicitly.

proof.text:
We now prove the required equality on every element, using the fraction model [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Since $c\notin\mathfrak q'$, for any $d\in C$ and $m\ge0$ we have $d/c^m\in\mathfrak q'C_c$ if and only if $d\in\mathfrak q'$. For the only nontrivial direction, express ideal membership as a finite sum with numerators in $\mathfrak q'$, put this sum over a common power of $c$, and use the fraction-equality rule to multiply the resulting equality by another power of $c$. It follows that $c^N d\in\mathfrak q'$ for some $N$; primality and $c\notin\mathfrak q'$ give $d\in\mathfrak q'$. Every $b\in B$ has the form $[P]/\bar g^{\,m}$. For this element the explicit map formula of Step 6, the kernel computation of Step 3, and the coefficient/evaluation identity of Step 5 give
$$\varphi(b)\in\mathfrak q'C_c\ \Longleftrightarrow\ P(\alpha)\in\mathfrak q'\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \rho(P)(a)=0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ h\mid\rho(P)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ b\in\mathfrak q.$$
The penultimate equivalence is Step 7; the last is the membership clause of [lem-trf-localized-fibre-prime-factor] used in Step 4. This proves $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q'C_c)=\mathfrak q$ in the original localized rings.

proof.text: The preceding construction works for every pair of primes over a common contraction, and the zero-ring case already supplied the allowed rank $r=0$. For nonzero $R$ the construction has $r\ge1$, including constant monic polynomials (where the factorization is the empty product and there are no primes of $B$ when the quotient is zero). This proves all clauses, including the explicitly allowed zero-ring and constant-polynomial edge cases.

lean.statement: theorem standardEtale_finiteFree_primeLifts {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (f g : R[X]) (hf : f.Monic) (hunit : IsUnit (((algebraMap (R[X] ⧸ Ideal.span ({f} : Set R[X])) (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({f} : Set R[X])) g))).comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({f} : Set R[X])))) f.derivative)) : ∃ (C : CommRingCat.{u}) (r : ℕ) (_ : Algebra R C), Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin r) R C) ∧ (Nontrivial R → 1 ≤ r) ∧ Surjective (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R C))) ∧ (∀ (q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({f} : Set R[X])) g))) (q' : PrimeSpectrum C), Ideal.comap (algebraMap R (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({f} : Set R[X])) g))) q.asIdeal = Ideal.comap (algebraMap R C) q'.asIdeal → ∃ (c : C), c ∉ q'.asIdeal ∧ ∃ (φ : Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({f} : Set R[X])) g) →ₐ[R] Localization.Away c), Ideal.comap (φ.toRingHom) (Ideal.map (algebraMap C (Localization.Away c)) q'.asIdeal) = q.asIdeal)
